title: Responsible AI Policy | Crenosoft
desc: How Crenosoft builds and uses AI responsibly: human oversight, transparency, privacy, accuracy testing and the AI we won’t build.
lead: We build AI that people can trust. This policy sets out the principles we follow in every system we build and run for clients, and in the AI we use ourselves.
body:
Our commitment

AI is now part of how Australian businesses answer customers, process work and make decisions. That makes how it is built and run as important as what it does. Our approach follows Australia’s AI Ethics Principles, the six essential practices in the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption, and the OAIC’s guidance on privacy and commercially available AI products.

1. People stay in control

Every system we build has a clear point where a person takes over. AI handles routine work; people make decisions that significantly affect someone, such as decisions about employment, credit, health or legal matters. In our human-backed AI Employees service, a dedicated Crenosoft team reviews exceptions, and business decisions are escalated to our client.

2. We are transparent about AI

People should know when they are dealing with AI. The AI receptionists, voice agents and chatbots we build tell users they are speaking with an AI assistant and always offer a way to reach a person. Our own website assistant is clearly labelled as AI.

3. Privacy by design

We give AI systems access only to the information they need. We do not enter personal or sensitive information into public AI tools. We configure AI providers so client data is not used to train public models where that option exists, use Australian hosting regions where available, and handle any overseas access in line with Australian Privacy Principle 8. Details are in our Privacy Policy.

4. Accuracy is tested, not assumed

Before launch, we test each system on real examples from the client’s business, including difficult cases, and measure how often it gets the right answer. After launch, we review samples of its work every month and fix problems at the cause. AI answers are grounded in approved sources wherever possible, and systems are designed to say “I don’t know” rather than guess.

5. Fairness and avoiding harm

We consider who could be affected by a system and how. We check for outcomes that could unfairly disadvantage people, design for accessibility, and avoid using AI to make sensitive judgements about individuals without human review.

6. Security

AI systems are secured like any other business system: least-privilege access, encrypted connections, secure credential storage, logging and monitoring, and protections against prompt manipulation and data leakage.

7. Accountability

Every system we build has a named owner on our team and on the client’s side, documentation of what it does and what data it uses, and a record of changes. Clients receive regular reports on performance, exceptions and improvements.

What we won’t build

  • AI designed to deceive people about whether they are dealing with a person
  • Deepfakes or impersonation of real people without their consent
  • Covert surveillance or monitoring of individuals
  • Systems that make final decisions about people’s employment, credit, health, housing or legal rights without meaningful human review
  • Marketing or outbound calling that ignores consent or opt-out requirements

How we use AI internally

Our team uses approved AI tools for drafting, coding and analysis under an internal usage policy. Client confidential information is only used in tools approved for that purpose, and every AI-assisted deliverable is reviewed by a person before it reaches a client.

Questions and concerns

If you have a question about how we use AI, or a concern about a system we have built, please contact us at [contact email]. We review this policy at least once a year and whenever Australian guidance changes.
